title: The WhataHotel Take: Il San Pietro di Positano

turns.speaker: advisor
turns.name: Luxury Advisor
turns.text: Il San Pietro di Positano is a Relais & Châteaux hotel terraced down a cliff just outside town. Understand the cliff, and you understand the stay.

turns.speaker: traveler
turns.name: Candid Traveler
turns.text: Starting with that little chapel at the top.

turns.speaker: advisor
turns.name: Luxury Advisor
turns.text: A 17th-century chapel to San Pietro marks the entrance. Below it, every room has a private sea-view terrace, and an elevator carved into the rock drops you to the private beach and Carlino restaurant.

turns.speaker: advisor
turns.name: Luxury Advisor
turns.text: That's the thing. Zass holds one Michelin star, and ten organic garden terraces supply the kitchens. In season there's a complimentary late-morning boat cruise with swimming.

turns.speaker: advisor
turns.name: Luxury Advisor
turns.text: Honeymooners, couples, and food lovers. Between the heated pool, the spa with its hammam and a tennis court between the cliffs, you'll happily stay put.

turns.speaker: traveler
turns.name: Candid Traveler
turns.text: My caution: it's seasonal, generally April to October, and children need to be ten or older. The coast road from Naples can also be congested.

turns.speaker: advisor
turns.name: Luxury Advisor
turns.text: True, so take the car-plus-boat transfer the concierge arranges. And town is a few minutes away on the free 24-hour shuttle.

turns.speaker: traveler
turns.name: Candid Traveler
turns.text: Fair. Just expect elevators and stairs, and a shuttle for dinners in town. For couples who want serious food and a private beach, it's a beautiful fit.

turns.speaker: advisor
turns.name: Luxury Advisor
turns.text: With the WhataHotel Preferred Rate, you get free breakfast for two daily, free Wi-Fi, a priority upgrade if available at check-in, a $100 hotel credit, among other perks.

short_version.atmosphere: Cliffside terraces stepping down to a private beach
short_version.worth_knowing: Seasonal, generally April to October; ages 10 and up; shuttle into town
